key_insight: REACT uses semantic contact supervision and generative partner-state modeling to enable humanoid–human interactions despite severe visual occlusion.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports contact-rich humanoid control using onboard sensing alone, without requiring external tracking or privileged human state at deployment.
method: Use a vision-language model to identify semantic contacts in human demonstrations and retarget them to humanoid–human geometry.
Train privileged interaction policies with contact-aware rewards, then distill them into egocentric depth policies using photorealistic human depth rendering.
Train generative partner-state models to predict partner motion from occluded onboard views.
evidence_signal: Across five interactions evaluated in simulation and on a Unitree G1, partner-state modeling improved contact recall in four, and the real robot performed all five using onboard sensing alone.
watch_item: Evaluation covers only five interactions, leaving generalization to unseen contact patterns and sensing conditions uncertain.
paper_title: VLM-Guided Contact Retargeting and Generative Partner Modeling for Humanoid-Human Interaction
